title: Sparrow Foundry on‑prem blueprint + TF stubs and rollout plan
content:
Status: working draft — internal; notes from design syncs 11/15 → 11/28

Project: Sparrow Foundry (manufacturing analytics) — private on‑prem deployment prototype
Owner: Sparrow Foundry infra lead TBD (we have initial contact: anna.kovacs@sparrowfoundry.com)
Redwood lead: Maya Chen (eng‑private‑deploy)
Goal: Deliver a low-latency inference footprint inside Sparrow Foundry's datacenter for real‑time QC and alerting pipelines. Initial target: 95th p50 latency < 120ms for 64-token gen calls at 50 concurrent sessions; sustained throughput for batched inference 200 qps for embeddings and reranking.

Scope (what this doc covers):
- Network topology and minimal on‑prem hardware sizing for an MVP cluster
- Terraform module skeletons and variable choices for Sparrow's environment
- Upgrade/patch plan and rollback checklist for both infra (TF) and runtime (model/runtime images)
- Acceptance tests and validation plan
- Open questions and assumptions to validate with Sparrow infra team

Constraints / customer facts collected so far (from discovery call 11/6):
- On‑prem colo, private VLANs; egress to Redwood control plane allowed via specific proxy (https outbound only, port 443); no incoming holes preferred
- Storage: 200TB NFS available, 10Gbps connectivity between compute racks
- Existing orchestration: VMware vSphere for VM life cycle; Sparrow is open to a small Kubernetes cluster (k0s) managed by Redwood agent for runtime nodes
- Security: Sparrow will require KMS integration (Azure KeyVault) and FIPS‑compliant SSH bastion for any jump hosts

Key assumptions (please review and mark any you disagree with):
1) Customer will provision at least 4 x A100 40GB (or similar Ampere GPUs) nodes for MVP serving; Redwood runtime can multiplex across GPUs for model variants.
2) Control plane (Redwood private control plane component) will be allowed outbound to redwood-cloud endpoints via proxy; no direct inbound webhooks required.
3) Customer will run a lightweight k8s control plane (3 control VMs) and allow Redwood to manage worker nodes as VMs via Terraform modules.
4) NFS will be used for large model artifacts (shared read‑only mounts) and local NVMe per node for KV cache.
5) Networking supports jumbo frames between GPUs (recommended) and can provide /21 for cluster pods.

Recommended architecture (textual diagram):
- Customer network VLANs: mgmt / control / worker / storage / bastion
- Terraform creates: vSphere resource pool → 3 control plane VMs → 6 worker VMs (4 GPU, 2 CPU for autoscaling/routing)
- Kubernetes nodes: 3 control (k0s), 4 gpu-workers (each with 1 GPU, 2x40GB A100 or 1xA100 plus 1xT4 for batching), 2 infra-non-gpu workers (prometheus, ingress, sidecars)
- Storage: NFS mount exported to all nodes for model artifacts; per‑node NVMe mounted at /var/lib/redwood/cache
- Networking: internal LB (HAProxy) on infra workers, NAT via bastion for outbound control plane egress

Sizing rationale (MVP):
- Model: Llama‑style 34B quantized variant for production-like quality testing
- Token profile: 64 average request, 512 max sequence in tails
- Concurrency target: 50 interactive sessions → estimate 4 GPU nodes gives headroom for batching and KV cache reuse for prefix reuse workloads
- CPU/RAM per GPU node: 64 vCPU, 512GB RAM (to hold memory-mapped quantized weights & KV cache staging). If customer can supply 80–96 vCPU that is even better.
- Storage: 1.5TB NVMe per GPU node for caching; 50–100GB local root for logs/monitoring

Terraform module notes (TF stubs + recommended variables):
- Module naming: redwood-sparrow/vsphere-cluster (root), redwood-sparrow/vm-gpu-pool, redwood-sparrow/networking, redwood-sparrow/k0s-bootstrap
- Variables to parameterize: vsphere_datacenter, vsphere_cluster, vm_template_id, gpu_type (A100-40GB), gpu_count_per_node, storage_nfs_export, bastion_ssh_pubkey, outbound_proxy_url, azure_kv_endpoint
- Outputs: control_plane_ips, gpu_node_ips, nfs_mount_path, tfstate_backend_bucket (customer-managed S3/minio)
- Notes on idempotency: avoid writing dynamic bootstrap secrets directly into TF outputs; inject ephemeral secrets via k8s secrets manifest applied by CI/CD pipeline after node creation.
- Minimal TF flow: plan -> apply (creates VMs + network) -> run remote-exec to install k0s + CNI + Redwood agent -> apply k8s manifests for runtime.
- TF state: recommend remote state in guarded S3 with MFA and prefix per environment (prod/staging). We will provide sample backend config.

Runtime / image upgrade and rollback plan (high level):
Preconditions: health checks green, canary pool configured (1 GPU node can be a canary), artefacts stored with immutable tags.
1) Build new runtime image + push to customer's registry (image: redwood/runtime:sparrow‑20251120)
2) Deploy to canary node (taint other nodes) and run smoke tests (latency sample, infer end‑to‑end with trace logging)
3) If tests pass, rollout 25% of GPU nodes, monitor metrics for 30–60 minutes (latency, error rate, token throughput).
4) Continue 50% → 100% if stable. If regressions observed, automatic rollback to prior image on affected nodes and trigger incident runbook.
Rollback checklist (quick):
- Pause ingress to canary nodes
- Revert runtime image tag in k8s deployment
- Restart pods with zero‑downtime draining and warmup KV cache sequence
- Verify token per-second metrics return to baseline
- Run a postmortem; capture debug artifacts (Gcore, traces)

Acceptance tests / SRE checks for cutover:
- Smoke: example prompt set (10 prompts) run end‑to‑end with < 150ms p50 on 64-token average (canary)
- Load: synthetic load hitting 200 qps for embeddings and 50 concurrent interactive sessions for 30 minutes with <1% errors
- Security: no outbound connections except allowed proxy; registry pull happens only from customer registry
- Observability: Prometheus job scraping, Grafana dashboard present, alert for GPU OOM/evictions

Operational runbook snippets (quick hits):
- Node replacement: use TF to provision replacement VM, cordon + drain old node, delete old instance from TF state after replacement verified
- Quick capacity burst: add prebuilt VM template into vm-gpu-pool with variable burst_count; apply TF to create burst nodes then scale down after traffic subsides
- KV cache warmup: run replay tool (redwood-kv-replay) against models to prepopulate cache on new nodes during maintenance window

Open questions (must confirm with Sparrow):
- Do they prefer bare metal servers or GPU‑enabled VMs under vSphere? Bare metal would affect network SR‑IOV and perf tuning.
- Which identity provider will they use for control plane OAuth (OKTA, Azure AD)?
- Can we create an outbound TLS inspection exception for redwood control plane IPs (proxy) to allow long‑lived websocket/control connections?
- Do they require FIPS validated binaries and images? (affects packaging and runtime flags)

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: NFS bandwidth contention for model reads — mitigate by sharding model artifacts across multiple NFS exports and using aggressive local caching during first pulls
- Risk: vSphere template heterogeneity — mitigate by publishing required VM spec matrix and running preflight checks (disk, cpu, iommu) via remote-exec
- Risk: Upgrade rollback complexity — mitigate by automated canary + circuit breaker; keep last two image revisions available

Immediate next steps / owners:
- Maya: produce TF module skeletons and push initial PR for review (ETA 11/21) — see linked PR stub (linked artifact)
- Diego: follow up with Sparrow on GPU machine type (baremetal vs VM) and outbound proxy constraints (ETA 11/18)
- Sparrow infra (Anna): confirm KMS endpoint and whether registry is customer-managed (ETA 11/20)
- Priya: prepare acceptance test harness (prompts + load scripts) and share runbook snippets (ETA 11/24)

Notes / TODOs (rough):
- TODO: Add explicit example Terraform module snippets (variables.tf, main.tf skeleton) into repo PR — include sample taints for canary nodes.
- TODO: Add network MTU testing checklist for jumbo frames and verify 10Gbps interconnect on bench test
- TODO: Add section on licensing export controls for model artifacts (customer requested clarification)

Appendix: quick TF variable example (sketch)
- variable "gpu_node_count" { default = 4 }
- variable "gpu_type" { default = "A100-40GB" }
- variable "outbound_proxy" { default = "https://proxy.sparrow.internal:443" }
- module "gpu_pool" { source = "./modules/vm-gpu-pool" gpu_type = var.gpu_type count = var.gpu_node_count }

Last notes: this doc is intentionally high‑level to align with customer's not-yet-finalized constraints. Once Sparrow confirms baremetal vs VM and registry/KMS choices we will finalize the TF design and produce a step‑by‑step runbook with explicit commands and scripts (ansible/remote-exec) for the bootstrap path.
